candidates.label: Askar
candidates.support: Askar is a modern village near the traditional location of Jacob's Well, close to Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, and is the identification OpenBible.info's catalog records as the modern candidate for Sychar; its name is often compared to Sychar itself.

candidates.label: Shechem (Tell Balata)
candidates.support: Some scholarship treats Sychar as a variant name for, or a place very near, the ancient city of Shechem, whose remains lie at Tell Balata about a kilometre southwest of Askar; OpenBible.info's ancient-place catalog records this identification as an alternative for Sychar's ancient-name resolution.

summary.text: Sychar is the Samaritan town where, according to John's Gospel, Jesus met a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well. Its precise location is debated: some identify it with the modern village of Askar, others with the ancient city of Shechem at nearby Tell Balata.

scripture.textWEB: So he came to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

otConnections.note: John 4:5 explicitly recalls this plot of ground near Shechem that Jacob gave to his son Joseph, tying the Gospel scene to the patriarchal narrative.
